clue.text: Puffer train driver's tea …

indicators.note: to train is to shape or discipline, so the letters of the following words are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A railway driver's cup of tea, with a puffer train being an old steam engine, trailing off into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train' looks like part of 'Puffer train', but it is the anagram signal working on DRIVERSTEA. The ellipsis carries the sentence into 6 Across.
explanation.definitionFit: A puffer is one who puffs, that is praises or promotes, something, which is what a promoter of goods does.

clue.text: Crown owns Gatcombe Park … odd bits of it

indicators.note: to park something is to set it aside, here applied to the odd letters
the odd-numbered letters of the word are the ones set aside, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: Royalty owns Princess Anne's Gloucestershire estate, but only scattered parts of it.
explanation.walkthrough: Gatcombe Park is Princess Anne's country home. 'Park' looks like part of the name, but means set aside: drop G, T, O, B and keep the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The crown of something is its highest point or peak, its summit.

clue.text: Rome's authority imposes tax on international tin

parts.note: VAT is value added tax, a UK sales tax
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: The Roman government levies a duty on imported tin.
explanation.definitionFit: The Holy See, the Pope's government in Rome, is commonly referred to by the name of its city-state.

clue.text: Ride wave on mat

parts.note: a roller is a long swelling wave
a coaster is a small mat for a glass

explanation.surface: Surf a wave while standing on a mat.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairground ride on a steep, twisting track is this attraction.

clue.text: I'll depart but this individual won't!

definitions.text: I'll depart but this individual won't!

parts.words: I'll depart but this individual won't!
parts.note: the speaker admits they will die one day, while the being described never will; read the answer as two words, a contraction plus an adjective, to see the speaker's admission

explanation.surface: A speaker saying they will leave, though someone else will stay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depart' means die: someone who will die is mortal, and the one who never will is the opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: A being who never dies, like a god, is undying and everlasting.

clue.text: Prompt, say, getting grand playing

parts.note: e.g., for example, is signalled by say
G is short for grand, a thousand pounds
a play that is playing is on

explanation.surface: A cue, for instance, getting a thousand while performing.
explanation.definitionFit: To prompt someone is to urge or encourage them on.

clue.text: … perhaps eaten partly in recess?

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Continuing 1 Across, the tea is perhaps eaten partly during a break period.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is a vaulted recess or alcove at the end of a church, so it names a kind of recess.

clue.text: Expert on pipe work

parts.note: a pro is a professional, an expert
a duct is a pipe or channel

explanation.surface: A specialist working on the plumbing.
explanation.definitionFit: A product is a thing made, a piece of work or output.

clue.text: See about the placing of English players on pitch — that's fundamental

indicators.note: about places the cathedral word around the other pieces

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city, a bishop's see
men are players in a team
tar is pitch, the black sticky substance

explanation.surface: Look at the way English players are positioned on the field: that's basic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a verb; it is a bishop's diocese, Ely in Cambridgeshire. 'pitch' is tar, not a playing field.
explanation.definitionFit: Elementary means basic or rudimentary, the most fundamental level.

clue.text: Maybe copper can place landing point within mile

indicators.note: to place one thing in another is to set it there, starting the insertion
within says the second piece sits inside the first

parts.note: ML is a dictionary abbreviation for mile
ETA, estimated time of arrival, is the moment a flight lands

explanation.surface: Could a police officer fit a landing spot within a mile?
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' suggests a police officer; here it is the element, and 'Maybe' marks it as one example. 'can' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Copper is one example of a metal, hence the 'Maybe' marking the definition by example.

clue.text: Return last of stale crumbles a treasure found in Walmart?

indicators.note: Return says the whole string of pieces that follows is read from the far end back
last of picks the final letter of the word stale

parts.note: something that crumbles rots, decaying away
a treasure is a gem, as in a person who is a real gem

explanation.surface: Stale goods that crumble are sent back, and a treasure turns up in a US supermarket chain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return' looks like a shop refund but signals reading EROTSAGEM backwards. 'found in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Walmart is a giant US retailer, an example of a vast store selling everything; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: Her chocolates embarrassed young tutor

indicators.note: embarrassed implies being thrown into disarray, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A young teacher is flustered by her chocolates.
explanation.definitionFit: A school teacher instructs children, so a tutor of the young.

clue.text: An objective for students before uni, and their employment afterwards?

definitions.text: An objective for students before uni, and their employment afterwards?

parts.words: An objective for students before uni, and their employment afterwards?
parts.note: Clearing is the UK late-admissions system that matches school-leavers to spare university places; a house is where students may later live, so the clue reads the phrase as those two stages

explanation.surface: What school-leavers aim for before university, and what work they find after.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, Clearing is the scramble for remaining university places after exam results; the clue splits the phrase into that and a later stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A clearing house is a central agency handling transactions or information between parties, a job a graduate might take afterwards.

clue.text: Hitches gang finds a cause of anguish

parts.note: a hitchhiker thumbs a lift, so hitches equals thumbs
a crew is a gang

explanation.surface: A hitchhiking gang turns up trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: The medieval torture device that crushed digits caused agony, so a cause of anguish.

clue.text: Worker caught with drink gaining minimal approval

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
to lap is to drink as a cat does

explanation.surface: A labourer caught having a drink wins barely any approval.
explanation.definitionFit: A single clap of the hands is the smallest possible show of applause, so faint praise.

clue.text: Tacky note put forward about head of technology

indicators.note: about places the first piece around the next one

parts.note: to posit is to put forward an idea

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of the word technology

explanation.surface: A cheap, tasteless note proposed regarding the head of the tech department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tacky' suggests vulgar; here it means sticky.
explanation.definitionFit: A Post-it is a small sticky note, so tacky in the sense of adhesive.

clue.text: Throne spotted on summit of Dartmoor — that's an unexplained thing

parts.note: throne is a jokey name for the toilet, the loo
spotted means seen

indicators.note: summit of picks the first, top letter of Dartmoor in a down clue

explanation.surface: A throne is seen on a Dartmoor hilltop, a mystery.
explanation.walkthrough: Dartmoor is a national park of moorland in Devon.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose end is a detail left unresolved or unexplained.

clue.text: Cinematography's ruined phonetic language such as this

indicators.note: ruined says the letters of the long word are wrecked and rebuilt, after the second word's letters are taken away

parts.note: the long word taken whole, its 's standing for 'is' as a link

explanation.surface: Film-making has spoiled a sound-based language like this one.
explanation.walkthrough: CINEMATOGRAPHY less the letters of PHONETIC leaves MAGRAY, which 'ruined' rearranges; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hungarian, the Magyar tongue, is spelt very nearly as it sounds, so it is a phonetic language.

clue.text: Golf ranges encompassing ordinary scores

parts.note: G is Golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: encompassing means surrounding, so the ranging word goes around the letter

parts.note: to range is to rove or wander

explanation.surface: Golf driving ranges full of average scores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scores' suggests points, but here means scratches or cuts.
explanation.definitionFit: To score a surface is to cut lines into it, and such cut lines are grooves.

clue.text: Promoter's backing from pilot about right

definitions.note: read as 'promoter is', the 's working as a link

indicators.note: backing says the word for from is turned back to front

parts.note: from is OF, as in 'made of wood'

indicators.note: about puts the piloting word around the letter for right

parts.note: to pilot a vessel is to steer it

explanation.surface: A promoter's support comes from a pilot regarding what is right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' poses as support for the promoter but is the reversal signal; 'about' is the container signal for the right letter. The 's on 'Promoter' reads as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To foster an idea is to encourage and promote it, so one who fosters is a promoter.

clue.text: Revolt briefly over 'fragrance' in dish

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a rise, or rising, is a revolt
otto, also attar, is a fragrant oil from rose petals

explanation.surface: A short revolt over perfume in a dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' in a down clue puts RIS above OTTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is an Italian rice dish.

clue.text: Highlights of the movie business?

parts.note: stars being filmed are the film industry's highlights, while meteors are bright lights moving across the sky

explanation.surface: The best moments in the film industry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movie' is read as moving: meteors are moving lights in the sky, while film actors on set are stars being filmed.
explanation.definitionFit: Meteors streaking across the night sky are popularly called by this name, briefly bright lights in motion.

clue.text: Green water welling up

indicators.note: welling up in a down clue means the word rises, reading from the bottom

parts.note: Evian is a brand of bottled mineral water

explanation.surface: An inexperienced person tearing up, water welling.
explanation.definitionFit: Green means inexperienced or gullible, which is the sense of unsophisticated innocence.

clue.text: Trip flap

definitions.meaning: a short ride or jaunt, as in going for a quick drive
a state of panic, as in getting into a flat ...

explanation.surface: Stumble and panic.
explanation.definitionFit: A spin is a brief outing, and a flat spin is a state of agitation or fluster.

clue.text: Bank setter's entered: 'Red, sir, unfortunately'

indicators.note: entered says the setter's piece goes into the jumbled letters
unfortunately suggests things gone awry, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the setter speaking of themself: setter has, I've

explanation.surface: The setter has gone into a bank, sadly addressing a red-faced gentleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' suggests money, but it is a river's edge. 'unfortunately' is the anagram signal on 'Red, sir', and 'entered' says the setter's contribution goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A river's bank is the land alongside it, the waterside.

clue.text: Once trendy, you French admitted being agitated

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: hep is an old-fashioned word for fashionable, a forerunner of hip
tu is the French familiar word for you

explanation.surface: A formerly stylish person let in a French friend and became flustered.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a state, worked up or flustered, is to be agitated.

clue.text: Understanding is pervading our group

indicators.note: pervading means spreading through, so the word is sits inside the group word

parts.note: our group is we, the first person plural

explanation.surface: Insight is spreading among our team.
explanation.definitionFit: Understanding as an adjective means sagacious, knowing and sensible, which is what a sage person is.

clue.text: Cut one tendril off

indicators.note: off means gone bad or out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to snip away a single plant tendril.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like the gardener's instruction but is the definition, a cut of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenderloin is a prime cut of beef or pork from the loin.
